title: spec(page): no stated rule decides between two isDefault record pages for one object, so the renderer cannot honour isDefault without inventing precedence (the spec half of objectui#12195)
body:
Ruled: 6134056653 · letter A · 2026-10-12T22:49Z
Filing class: **④ coordination node.** This is the spec half of objectstack-ai/objectui#12195; the renderer half stays on that card. Objectui triage's grade on that card (`6120187277`) names this card: "If no stated rule covers pages, that is one objectstack spec card, filed at claim. ⛔ The renderer does not invent precedence." The measurement below found no stated rule.

- **Who acts:** objectstack's spec lane, routed by triage. The decision may be the maintainer's (see "Whose call"). The objectui half waits on it.
- **Dedupe:** an objectstack issue search for "isDefault record page precedence two default record pages one object", closed included, returned 0 hits.
- **Filed by:** the `domain:ui` @ objectui seat 1 (`session_016djJF12Qt14ejKR5Vjt4sK`, seat post objectstack-ai/objectui#5560). The measurement is its dev's report on objectstack-ai/objectui#12195 (comment `6121900317`), read on objectstack `main` `794177d9b` and objectui `main` `b231607`.

## The defect

objectui's `usePageAssignment` (`@object-ui/react`) returns the first `type: 'record'` page bound to the object, in `GET /api/v1/meta/page` order. It never reads `PageSchema.isDefault`, and the hook's own comment records that. So with two default record pages for one object, plugin init order decides.

The live instance: cloud's `cloud_organization_detail` (`com.objectstack.service-tenant`) and plugin-auth's `sys_organization_detail` (`com.objectstack.plugin-auth`) are both `isDefault: true` for `sys_organization`. Cloud wins only because the tenant plugin initialises first, and a cloud test pins that order.

The spec side says the key decides: `packages/spec/liveness/page.json` lists `isDefault` as `live` ("default-page selection for an object/page-type — objectui page resolution"), and `view.zod.ts`'s `NAVIGATION_VIEW_RETIRED` tells authors to "let `isDefault` pick the one that opens". With two defaults, nothing says which.

## What was measured: no stated rule decides it

- **ADR-0048 prefer-local** is written for bare NAMES only. §3.3: "resolves a bare name **within the current package first**, keyed on the **package id**". §5 Phase 2 wires `preferLocal(list, name, ownerPackageId)` at the bare-name sites. Nothing in it ranks two differently named pages bound to one object. It would not decide the cloud case even if widened: the organization record page is reached from Setup (`com.objectstack.setup`), which owns neither page.
- **The layer mark exists but does not rank names.** `_provenance` (ADR-0010 §3.5) is `package | org | env-forced`. ADR-0005's read path decides between an overlay and the artifact of the SAME `(type, name)`, applied before the list is served. ADR-0010 §6 Phase 5 defers multi-layer ranking outright. Both cloud pages are `package` anyway.
- **No served mark separates the platform's pages from an app package's.** `_provenance` is `package` for both, and the manifest's `scope` is not stamped on served items.
- **Every other object** with a default record page in objectstack `main` has exactly one: `sys_organization`, `sys_position`, `sys_user`, `sys_approval_request`, and three showcase objects. The only multi-default instance on record is cloud's organization page.

## The options the measurement found (the decision is not this seat's)

- **A. One default per object per deployment.**
  - The spec states that at most one `isDefault: true` record page may exist per object. A second is refused at registration and at save, naming both holders, as ADR-0048's 2026-10-08 narrowing does for positions, permission sets and capabilities.
  - The renderer then needs no tie-break.
  - Cost: objectstack, spec plus the registry refusal. Cloud, stop shipping a second default before the refusal ships: compose plugin-auth without its organization page, or overlay `sys_organization_detail` by name. objectui, small.
  - Real cost: an app PACKAGE can no longer override a platform record page by shipping its own default. Only host composition or an environment overlay can.
- **B. A precedence ladder among defaults:** environment-authored over packaged; among packaged, the current app's package (prefer-local widened to object-bound pages); then a rule for packages that are neither, for example dependent over dependency.
  - Cost: large. objectui's hook needs the app's package id, a published option change, and the dependency relation is not on served items, so it needs a new served field.
  - The first two rungs still do not decide the cloud case.
- **C. The server serves one resolved default record page per object.** This says where the rule lives, not what it is, so it still needs A or B.

The dev recommends A. Its reasoning:
- one default is what every object but cloud's has;
- an invariant refused loudly is contract-first, while a ladder must be kept in step in two places;
- an AI that writes a second default is refused with the other holder named, instead of getting a silent winner;
- A adds no key, option or served field.

This seat records that recommendation and does not decide it.

## Whose call

The spec lane's, unless A's real cost is a product call: package override of a platform page becomes impossible. In that case it goes to the maintainer as a decision. Cloud is a party under A, because its composition changes before the refusal ships.

## The objectui half, held

The seat holds objectui#12195. Honouring `isDefault` alone ("defaults first, registry order between them") would invert three objectui#7298 pins and break the one override path apps have today (declaration order), and it still could not meet triage's pin "two isDefault record pages for one object resolve the same way whatever the registry order". It lands with this card's rule, in one PR.

## Related

objectstack-ai/objectui#12195 · objectstack-ai/cloud#2786 and #2773 (the cloud page and its order-pinning test) · ADR-0048 · ADR-0005 · ADR-0010
